In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a behavioral intervention to reduce excessive weight gain in pregnancy.
the development and evaluation of an intervention to reduce excessive weight gain during the first pregnancy in low-income, normal weight and overweight women.
the prevention of excessive weight gain among low-income women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study demonstrated that a stepped-care intervention was effective in reducing excessive weight gain in normal weight women.
the intervention reduced excessive weight gains during pregnancy among normal-weight women.
the intervention significantly decreased the proportion of normal-weight women exceeding the IOM recommendations for weight gain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed and tested an intervention that decreased weight gain among normal weight women during pregnancy and reduced postpartum weight gain.
the intervention was not effective in reducing excessive weight gain during the pregnancy in overweight women.
the intervention decreased the percentage of overweight women who exceeded the recommendations, but this was not a significant effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it’s possible for low-income women to have healthy pregnancies, to have babies with normal birth weights and to not gain too much weight during pregnancy.
it’s possible to help normal weight women to gain within the IOM guidelines.
it is possible to reduce weight gain during pregnancy, even among a low-income population, with a stepped care behavioral intervention that is feasible and acceptable to women.
